_evidence: Every real check class implements Zi28.ZB() returning a burp.Zf8g enum constant (some qualify it as burp.Zf8g.X, which required a second grep pass); toString() is literally 'this.ZB().name()' on every check class. Extracted by grepping both 'return Zf8g.X;' and 'return burp.Zf8g.X;' across out/clean/root. Cross-verified at runtime: CheckClassTracer.java (JDI, breakpoints Zi28.Zw/Zrm7.ZX on every loaded implementor) confirmed live class hits against a real licensed Burp Pro instance scanning a controlled multi-vulnerability demo target, and get_scanner_issues (Burp's own MCP server) confirmed the resulting IssueType names. Entries marked 'runtime_confirmed' had both a class-hit in the tracer log AND a matching scanner issue reported for the same demo-target request during the same session.
_prefix_meaning: APH = active-per-host scope, APR = active-per-request scope, APIP = active-per-insertion-point scope, APU = active-per-URL(backup-file) scope, APP = active-per-path scope. Two classes with the same catalog issue but different prefixes are the same issue dispatched at two different scopes (e.g. ASP.NET tracing enabled: APH_AspTracingAppLevel + APR_AspNetTracingEnabled).
